settings.models_heading: Popular Mickey Thompson models in Calgary
settings.intro_heading: Why we recommend Mickey Thompson in Calgary
settings.intro_richtext:
Mickey Thompson has been making off-road tires since 1962 — founded by a Bonneville Salt Flats record holder, which is the kind of pedigree that translates into tires Calgary off-roaders specifically ask for by name.

The Baja Boss A/T is 3PMSF-rated and aggressive enough for serious gravel and rocky trail work — but quiet enough that Calgary owners run it daily on Deerfoot. The asymmetric tread design pulls air through to keep highway noise civilized.

For pure mud-terrain duty, the Baja Boss M/T goes more aggressive — deeper tread, beefier sidewalls, three-ply construction. The Baja Legend EXP sits between the two: all-terrain capability with a slightly more aggressive shoulder than typical A/T tires.

Every Mickey Thompson we install gets the same balance, calibrated torque, and TPMS reset — and we price-match local Calgary competitors. Book installation or call (403) 452-4283.
settings.faq_heading: Mickey Thompson questions Calgary drivers ask
settings.cta_description: Most Baja Boss sizes in stock. Same-day install on confirmed bookings — price-matched against any local Calgary competitor.
settings.faq_1_q: Are Mickey Thompson Baja Boss tires 3PMSF rated?
settings.faq_1_a: The Baja Boss A/T carries the 3PMSF (three-peak mountain snowflake) symbol — meets Alberta's winter-tire law and the BC Highway 93 / Trans-Canada Banff winter-tire mandate. The Baja Boss M/T is a true mud-terrain (no 3PMSF), per industry convention for M/T tires.
settings.faq_2_q: Baja Boss A/T vs M/T — which one for daily Calgary driving?
settings.faq_2_a: Baja Boss A/T if you're 80%+ on pavement. The M/T is a serious off-road tire — louder on highway, faster wear on pavement. We recommend the A/T for daily-driven trucks and the M/T only if you spend real time off-road.
settings.faq_3_q: How much do Mickey Thompson tires cost in Calgary?
settings.faq_3_a: Baja Boss A/T ranges $480–$700 per tire depending on size. Common LT truck sizes (LT285/70R17, 33x12.50R20) run $550–$660. M/T runs about $20–80 more per tire than the A/T in matched sizes.
settings.faq_4_q: Will Mickey Thompson tires fit my stock truck?
settings.faq_4_a: Most stock half-ton trucks (F-150, Silverado 1500, Ram 1500, Tundra) need either a leveling kit or staying with P-metric / smaller LT sizes (LT265/70R17, P285/55R20). Tell us your year/make/model when booking and we'll confirm fitment before we install.
settings.faq_5_q: Can I get same-day install on Mickey Thompson?
settings.faq_5_a: Yes for stocked sizes if booked before midday. We stock common Baja Boss A/T sizes (LT275/70R18, LT285/70R17, 33x12.50R20). Bigger and lifted-truck sizes need a 60-minute slot — call (403) 452-4283 to confirm.
settings.faq_6_q: Does Prince Tires balance large lifted-truck tires?
settings.faq_6_a: Yes. Heavy aggressive-tread tires (Baja Boss M/T, KM3, etc.) sometimes need extra balance work. We use Hunter Road Force balancers, which compensate for tire/wheel match quality better than standard balancers — recommended for any tire over 35 inches or LT load ranges D/E.
settings.calgary_richtext: Mickey Thompson is our off-road specialist — Baja Boss A/T and Baja Boss M/T cover the oilfield, the Eastern Slopes, and any truck owner who wants a serious-looking stance. The MTZ P3 is a mud-terrain favourite for heavy 3/4-ton trucks. These aren't quiet tires, but for Calgary truck owners who actually leave pavement, nothing else looks or grips quite like them.
